limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose you have just participated in a school project of collecting used books on campus. You are now to write a report about the project, which may include its aim, organizers, participants and activities. You will have 30 minutes to write the report. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
title: A Report on the Used Book Collection Project
body: Recently, a used book collection project was carried out on our campus. As a volunteer, I would like to give a brief report on it.

The project was organized by the student union together with the university library. Its aim was to give used books a second life and to help children in need. Students and teachers from all departments were invited to take part, and more than two hundred volunteers helped with the work.

The activities lasted two weeks. During the first week, collection boxes were placed in every dormitory building and in the library, and volunteers went from room to room to collect textbooks, novels and reference books. In the second week, the volunteers sorted the books into different categories. The books were then sold cheaply at a campus book fair, and all the money raised was donated to a charity that supports disadvantaged children.
The project was a great success. It not only put unused books to good use but also showed participants how they could serve others.

limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt: Directions: Suppose your university student union is planning to hold a speech contest. You are now to write a proposal for organizing the contest. The proposal may include the topic, aim, procedure and selection of contestants. You will have 30 minutes to write the proposal. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
title: A Proposal for Organizing a Speech Contest
body: Our student union is planning to hold a speech contest this semester. Here is my proposal for organizing it.

The topic of the contest will be “My Dream and My Responsibility,” which encourages students to think about their goals and the role they can play in society. The aim is to improve students’ public speaking skills, build their confidence and make campus life more vibrant.

The contest will be open to all students, and contestants will be selected in two rounds. Each department will hold a preliminary round and recommend two speakers for the final. As for the procedure, the final will be held in the university auditorium in late November. Each contestant will give a five-minute prepared speech and then answer a question from the judges. A panel of teachers will score the speeches based on content, language and delivery, and the top three speakers will receive certificates and prizes.
The contest will be a valuable opportunity for students to show their talents and learn from one another. I hope my proposal will be helpful.

prompt: Directions: Suppose your school is organizing an orientation program to help the freshmen adapt to the new environment and academic studies. You are now to write a proposal, which may include its aim, duration, participants and activities. You will have 30 minutes to write the proposal. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
title: A Proposal for a Freshman Orientation Program
body: To help freshmen adapt to their new environment and academic studies as quickly as possible, I would like to propose an orientation program at the start of the coming semester.

The program will last one week, starting on the day after registration. It will be organized by the Student Affairs Office with the help of student volunteers, and all freshmen are expected to take part. Teachers from each department and senior students will also be invited.

The program will include a variety of activities. On the first day, freshmen will take a guided tour of the campus to become familiar with the library, laboratories, canteens and the medical center. Next, teachers will hold meetings to introduce the curriculum, credit requirements and effective study methods. Then senior students will share tips on balancing study and social life and answer questions in small groups. Finally, a welcome party will be held so that freshmen can make new friends.
I am confident that this program will help freshmen settle in smoothly and get off to a good start in college.

prompt:
Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled “Do violent video games lead to violence?”. The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.

A growing body of research finds that violent video games can make kids act aggressively in their real world relationships, causing an increase in violence.
title: Do violent video games lead to violence?
body: Many studies suggest that violent video games may make children more aggressive in real life. In my opinion, although such games alone seldom turn a person violent, they can indeed encourage aggressive behavior, especially among young players.

Children are still developing their sense of right and wrong. When they spend hours playing games in which fighting and killing are rewarded with points, they may come to see violence as an acceptable way to solve problems. Some may even copy the foul language and violent actions they see on the screen. Moreover, playing such games for long periods can make players less sensitive to the suffering of others.

Of course, violence has many causes, such as family problems and peer pressure, and not everyone who plays these games becomes violent. Still, the risks cannot be ignored. Parents should choose games suitable for their children’s age and limit their playing time, and game companies should take their social responsibility seriously. With such measures, young people can enjoy games without being harmed by them.

limit: at least 120 words but no more than 180 words
prompt:
Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled “Is technology making people lazy?”. The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.

Many studies claim that computers distract people, make them lazy thinkers and even lower their work efficiency.
title: Is technology making people lazy?
body: It is often claimed that computers leave people easily distracted, mentally lazy and less efficient at work. In my view, technology itself does not make people lazy; what matters is how they use it.

It is true that technology can encourage laziness. With search engines at hand, some people no longer bother to remember facts or think problems through. Others rely on navigation apps for every trip and rarely try to find their own way. Constant messages and pop-up advertisements also interrupt their work, making it hard to concentrate and lowering their efficiency.

On the other hand, technology can make people more productive when it is used wisely. It frees people from repetitive tasks such as calculating figures and copying documents, giving them more time for creative work. Online courses and digital libraries also allow them to learn new skills and explore new fields whenever and wherever they like. The key, therefore, is self-discipline. If people treat technology as a tool rather than a crutch, it will make them smarter, not lazier.

Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled “Are people becoming addicted to technology?”. The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.

Numerous studies claim that addiction to technology is real and it has the same effect on the brain as drug addiction.
title: Are people becoming addicted to technology?
body: Some researchers warn that heavy use of technology can affect the brain much as drugs do. When we look around, it is hard to disagree: many people today are indeed becoming addicted to technology.

Signs of this addiction are everywhere. On the subway, almost everyone is staring at a phone screen. At dinner, friends check their messages instead of talking to each other. Many students scroll through short videos late into the night and feel anxious whenever their phones are out of reach. One reason for this is that apps are designed to keep users hooked with endless updates, likes and notifications, which give people constant small rewards.

However, technology is not the enemy; the real problem is our lack of self-control. To avoid becoming slaves to technology, we should set limits on our screen time, turn off unnecessary notifications and spend more time on real-world activities such as reading, sports and face-to-face conversations with family and friends. Only when we stay in control can technology truly serve us.
